{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABbWQ2pw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhE69G0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 26, "title": "Speed up GitHub Pages deployment by separating full SNES tests from publishing", "body": "## Problem

The GitHub Pages workflow currently runs `npm test` as a prerequisite for uploading and deploying the static site on every push to `main`. That command runs Python service tests, trusted-local Playwright tests and the complete static browser suite, including expensive SNES compilation and cartridge checks in Chromium and Firefox.

As a result, merged features can remain absent from the public site for hours. The SNES merge (`f4ae6e4`) triggered [workflow run #41145188848](https://github.com/takahirox/webrtl/actions/runs/41145188848), which was still in the `Run npm test` step more than three hours after starting; neither the Pages artifact upload nor deployment had begun. This is a release-pipeline bottleneck, not a reason to bypass substantive pre-merge quality gates.

## Expected outcome

**Decouple quick GitHub Pages publication from the expensive full SNES regression suite.** Publish an already-reviewed `main` commit through a short, reproducible static build + targeted smoke test. Preserve thorough automated regression coverage in a separate PR/manual workflow, with clear results and no reduction of expected PR review quality.

## Implementation scope

- Split `.github/workflows/pages.yml` into a **fast Pages build/deploy path** and a **separate full validation path** (either separate workflow files or clearly separated jobs with correct event/dependency conditions).
- For `main` pushes, run `npm ci`, `npm run build:demo` and a bounded, appropriate static smoke check verifying the newly built `/webrtl/` artifact serves correctly, includes the current SNES example/ROM/UI assets, and that the basic browser application can load. Include a fresh browser-generated circuit check where practical; **do not run the full SNES cartridge sweep on the critical deployment path**.
- The Pages artifact must be the exact checked-out commit's tested build, not a stale/cached artifact or an untested different branch. Preserve the proper GitHub Pages artifact upload, permissions and deployment environment. Failed build or critical smoke test must prevent publishing.
- Run `npm test` and full Chromium/Firefox SNES regression suites in an independent workflow for PRs and `workflow_dispatch` (and optionally a scheduled run if useful), with actionable checks/statuses. Avoid needless duplicate full suites for the same commit. Describe how required checks should be configured or reviewed **without assuming that branch protection already exists**.
- Keep the existing `npm test` command usable for local and CI validation; split/add focused npm scripts only where they improve clarity. Preserve coverage for counter, CPU, BG1, audio/video and SNES in the full test path.
- Give the Pages workflow an explicit run summary (source commit, build/smoke results, artifact, deployment URL/status) and keep full-suite failures visible without silently blocking already reviewed publication. Avoid unbounded retries, concurrency starvation or canceling an in-progress deployment in a way that leaves the site outdated.
- Document what runs on PR versus `main` and how an operator can identify whether a merged SNES feature has been deployed; include a sensible deployment-duration target/measurement rather than assuming a fixed time.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] A push to `main` follows a short build → bounded smoke → upload → deploy dependency chain, **without `npm test` or the complete SNES multi-cartridge suite** on that chain.
- [ ] The deployed artifact is built from that push's commit and is checked for expected SNES example/source/ROM availability (not just an HTTP 200 on an old site). A deliberate missing SNES asset or broken static build blocks deployment in automated tests.
- [ ] A separate PR/manual full-validation workflow runs the existing comprehensive Python, trusted-local and static browser tests, including SNES Chromium/Firefox tests, and reports failures clearly. No tests are deleted merely to make deployment faster.
- [ ] Appropriate static/browser smoke testing remains on the deployment path; the complete suite still runs before merging via documented PR checks/review practice. Any needed repository-setting changes are documented, not claimed to have been applied without evidence.
- [ ] Demonstrate the workflow split using safe validation (workflow syntax/event checks, CI job results and/or dry-run-style tests). Record measured or defensible expected time for the fast path and distinguish it from full-suite runtime.
- [ ] Existing `npm run build:demo`, `npm test` and static GitHub Pages behavior are preserved; no application-level runtime refactor is introduced without necessity.

## Optional validation

- Compare GitHub Actions timings across a successful fast deployment and a full regression run; tune browser-worker parallelism in the full suite separately.
- Add a lightweight public-site post-deployment smoke check that verifies the deployed commit/example, while keeping extended ROM/pixel/audio/controller tests separate.

## Required post-merge verification

After merging this CI change, verify a **real `main` workflow** builds, passes the fast smoke, uploads and deploys the current SNES-capable site. Confirm the public Example selector exposes **`SNES · experimental base console RTL`** and record the deployment commit and elapsed time. Separately verify that the full PR/manual regression workflow can still execute and reports its result. Do not treat a successful local build as proof of live publication.
